title: Module 15 · Mixed Patients (Top 10%)
intro: Real patients cross modules. Each case stacks problems the way a night shift does: magnesium plus infection plus kidneys, sepsis plus renal dosing, a bleed caused by a dosing error, crush injury, DKA with QT risk, postpartum clots while breastfeeding, HIT history and falling platelets.

cases.title: Magnesium, fever and falling urine
cases.stem: On magnesium 2 g/h for 10 hours. Now temperature 39 °C, fetal tachycardia: intraamniotic infection. Urine output 20 mL/h for 3 hours, SCr up from 0.6 to 1.3. Weight 90 kg. No allergies.

steps.q: Before any antibiotic, what do you do about the magnesium?

options.t: Check reflexes, RR and Mg level; lower the rate
options.why: Label: renal impairment maintenance 1 g/h; hold if UO below 100 mL per 4 h.

options.t: Continue 2 g/h; UO above 15 mL/h is enough
options.why: Label requires 100 mL per 4 hours (25 mL/h).

options.t: Stop magnesium and give calcium gluconate 1 g
options.why: Calcium is for toxicity signs, which are not described yet.

options.t: Raise to 3 g/h now that fever is present
options.why: Accumulation risk with falling kidney function.

options.t: Ampicillin 2 g IV q6h plus gentamicin
Ampicillin 2 g IV q4h plus gentamicin
options.why: Every 4 hours is the meningitis interval.

options.t: Cefazolin 2 g IV q8h plus gentamicin
options.why: The alternative for mild penicillin allergy; she has none.

steps.q: How do falling kidney function and magnesium change your gentamicin thinking?

options.t: Use levels, not normal clearance; watch Mg synergy
options.why: Magnesium plus aminoglycosides both block the neuromuscular junction.

options.t: Hartford 7 mg/kg; SCr 1.3 is still normal
options.why: Rising SCr and low UO mean clearance is falling.

options.t: Gentamicin 5 mg/kg q24h; no levels needed
Double the gentamicin to overcome fever

cases.call: **S/B:** On magnesium 2 g/h, new intraamniotic infection, urine 20 mL/h, SCr 0.6 to 1.3. **A:** Magnesium is accumulating, and gentamicin adds kidney and neuromuscular risk. **R:** Magnesium level and reflex check now, lower magnesium to 1 g/h per label, start ampicillin 2 g q6h plus gentamicin with levels guided dosing, and I will follow her kidney function.
cases.pearl: **One patient, three risks: magnesium build up, aminoglycoside kidney injury, and stacked neuromuscular blockade.**

sources.t: Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose label (MedLibrary)
ACOG Committee Opinion 712: intrapartum management of intraamniotic infection. Obstet Gynecol 2017
Gentamicin injection prescribing information (DailyMed)

workup.calc: Urine 20 mL/h x 3 h (60 mL in 3 h, goal 75 mL) and SCr doubled: lower to 1 g/h per label, level now. Gentamicin adds kidney and neuromuscular risk.

cases.title: Septic shock with failing kidneys
cases.stem: Septic shock from a pneumonia, 80 kg, CrCl 25 mL/min. Norepinephrine 0.3 mcg/kg/min for 5 hours. Orders: vancomycin 1,000 mg, cefepime 2 g every 8 hours, pantoprazole.

options.why: Not reduced for kidneys; maintenance by kidneys and levels (Rybak 2020, max 3 g).
Loads are not reduced for kidneys.
Maintenance style dosing; too frequent for CrCl 25.

options.t: Full first dose now; adjust maintenance
Continue 2 g q8h for the whole course
Halve the first dose to 1 g now

options.why: Norepinephrine 0.25 or more for over 4 hours.

cases.pearl: **Septic shock + bad kidneys: full loads, adjust maintenance, steroids, vasopressin, SUP.**

sources.t: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021. Crit Care Med 2021;49:e1063-e1143
Rybak MJ, et al. Vancomycin consensus guideline. Am J Health Syst Pharm 2020;77:835-864
FDA safety alert: cefepime and nonconvulsive status epilepticus (2012)
SCCM/ASHP 2024 stress ulcer prophylaxis guideline

cases.title: The fall, the bleed, and what comes next
cases.setting: ED to neuro ICU · elderly woman
cases.stem: 84 years old, 58 kg, fell at home. ICH on CT. Apixaban 5 mg BID for AF (SCr 1.6). SBP 188.

options.why: ICH 2022; andexanet withdrawn from the US in 2025.

options.t: Vitamin K 10 mg IV; SBP below 110
options.why: Warfarin reversal; too low a BP target.

steps.q: Looking back at her home dose, what do you notice?

options.t: Should have been 2.5 mg BID (3 of 3 criteria)
options.why: Age 80+, weight 60 kg or less, SCr 1.5+.

options.t: Correct: only 2 of 3 criteria are met
Should have been stopped for SCr 1.6
options.why: Apixaban is still used; dose reduced.

options.t: 24 to 48 h after the bleed is stable
Never after any ICH, for life
options.why: VTE risk is high; prophylaxis is reasonable.
Treatment dose is a different decision.

cases.pearl: **Reverse, control BP, then find the error that set it up (wrong apixaban dose).**

cases.title: Crush injury, day 3
cases.stem: Crush injury 3 days ago. CK 48,000, K 6.8 with peaked T waves, urine output falling. On gentamicin for an open fracture. Now needs reintubation.

options.t: Calcium, then insulin + dextrose, then removal
options.why: Consider 5 units with kidney injury; binder, dialysis.

options.t: Calcium alone; it lowers the potassium
options.why: Calcium stabilizes but does not lower K.

options.t: Binder alone; it works within minutes
Insulin 20 units IV with no dextrose

options.why: Crush injury after 24 to 48 hours and K 6.8.

options.t: Ask for a non nephrotoxic option; levels if continued
Raise gentamicin for better bone penetration
Stop all antibiotics for the fracture

cases.pearl: **Crush day 3: no succinylcholine, treat K in 3 steps, and rethink nephrotoxins.**

cases.title: DKA with pneumonia
cases.stem: DKA, K 3.1, Mg 1.4, QTc 510. Chest X ray: lobar pneumonia, not severe. Orders: insulin drip, ceftriaxone, azithromycin, ondansetron.

options.t: No: replace K to 3.5+, and Mg, first
Yes: start insulin with KCl in the fluids
options.why: K below 3.5 risks arrhythmia with insulin.

options.t: Yes: K above 3.0 is enough to start
Yes: give a 10 unit bolus first
options.why: No bolus, and K is too low.

steps.q: What is the hidden danger in this order set?

options.t: QTc 510, low K and Mg, plus QT drugs
options.why: Azithromycin and ondansetron prolong QT: torsades risk.

steps.q: Which CAP option avoids adding QT risk?

options.why: ATS/IDSA alternative when a macrolide should be avoided.

cases.pearl: **Low K, low Mg, long QT: fix electrolytes, then choose drugs that do not stack QT.**

cases.title: Postpartum clot while breastfeeding
cases.stem: Day 4 after cesarean, new PE. Breastfeeding. BP 158/98 on two readings. Pain orders include acetaminophen with codeine.

steps.q: Which anticoagulants are compatible with breastfeeding?

options.why: ACOG; enalapril is compatible with breastfeeding.
ACE inhibitors are avoided in pregnancy, not postpartum.
Linked to postpartum depression; not first choice postpartum.
Scheduled acetaminophen and ibuprofen; short low dose oxycodone if needed (FDA 2017).

options.t: Fine at standard doses for 7 days
options.why: Ultrarapid metabolizers expose the infant to morphine.

options.t: Fine if the infant is over 1 week old
options.why: Risk at any age while breastfeeding.

options.t: Switch to tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours

cases.pearl: **Breastfeeding: enoxaparin or warfarin, labetalol or nifedipine or enalapril, no codeine.**

cases.title: Warfarin bleed in a patient with HIT history
cases.stem: GI bleed, INR 6.8 on warfarin. Allergy list: "heparin: HIT 2023."

options.t: No: Kcentra contains heparin; HIT contraindicates
Yes: heparin content is too small to matter
Yes: HIT from 2023 is no longer relevant
options.why: Label lists known HIT; follow policy.

options.t: Yes: if given with vitamin K
Vitamin K 10 mg IV plus plasma (FFP)
options.why: Team weighs volume; or a heparin free factor product if stocked.

options.t: Vitamin K 10 mg IV only; wait 24 hours

steps.q: Which other heparin exposures do you block for this patient?

options.t: Heparin flushes and heparin coated catheters

options.why: Used as an HIT alternative; little cross reactivity.

cases.pearl: **HIT history: no Kcentra, no heparin flushes, no enoxaparin.**

cases.title: Falling platelets on day 15
cases.stem: Day 15 of linezolid. On sertraline and heparin 5,000 units SC q8h since admission. Platelets 210,000 to 95,000. No new clot.

options.t: HIT possible; timing and other cause lower 4Ts

options.why: Possible but not a leading cause here.

steps.q: What else about linezolid and sertraline?

options.why: Linezolid is a weak MAO inhibitor; discuss with the team.

options.t: QT prolongation is the main concern
Score 4Ts, test if needed, ask ID
options.why: HIT testing if intermediate; ask ID about an alternative to linezolid.
No bleeding; platelets can worsen HIT clots.

options.t: Stop heparin and do nothing else

cases.pearl: **Low platelets: list every cause (drug, HIT, sepsis). Linezolid after 2 weeks is a classic.**
